3. AI is success, eventually leading to AGI, and a new industrial revolution, leaving hundreds of millions of blue collar workers without a job (plumbers, farmers just fine). Government launches Universal Basic Income to avoid revolt in the transition period until newly laid off can find a job. Fed steps in with unlimited debt monetization/YCC to prevent debt market collapse.

What else?

tweets.text:
Ben Horowitz on why asking whether AI is good or bad misses the point:

"I always like to go back to a quote from Andy Grove, which I absolutely love, which he said in the '90s. And somebody asked him, 'Andy, is the microprocessor good or bad?' And he said, 'Well, that's not even the right question. That's like asking, is steel good or bad? It is. And so it's our job to make it good.'"

"You can't get rid of the wheel now. It's over. It's here. You can't get rid of AI now. It's over. It's here. You can't outlaw math."

"So then the real question is, what do we have to do to make it good and positive for society? And by the way, without new technologies, how are we going to deal with pandemics or climate change or any of the real issues facing the world?"

@bhorowitz with @eriktorenberg on Turpentine VC, 2023

Investors are piling into leveraged semiconductor trades:

The 3x leveraged long semiconductor ETF, SOXL, has attracted +$1.9 billion in inflows so far this week.

On Monday alone, the fund recorded +$1.7 billion in inflows, its largest daily intake since November 6th.

This follows +$2.7 billion in inflows during the previous week, its 3rd-largest weekly intake since June.

Meanwhile, over the 20 trading days ended Friday, retail net purchases of SOXL rose to +$1.3 billion, the largest 20-day rolling sum since at least December 2024.

Furthermore, the semiconductor ETF, SMH, has attracted +$2.9 billion in inflows so far in November, on track for its biggest monthly intake since July and 3rd-largest since May 2023.

Investors are buying the dip in chip stocks on leverage.

tweets.text:
BREAKING: US new home sales jumped +14.2% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 701,000 units, the highest since December 2025, crushing expectations of a -3.8% decline.

This marks the largest monthly increase since November 2025 and the 2nd-largest since August 2022.

It also marks a sharp recovery from the -9.7% MoM decline in September.

October's surge was driven by sales in the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, which soared +36.2% MoM, to an annualized rate of 515,000 units, the highest since March 2021.

At the same time, the median new home sale price fell -0.3% MoM and -3.2% YoY, to $391,300, the 2nd-lowest reading since July 2021.

Since the October 2022 peak, the median new home sale price has declined by $69,000, or -15.0%.

New home prices are falling sharply.

Patrick Collison's advice to people in their 20s: find where the highest standards are, and go experience them firsthand.

"When I talk to people in other domains, this is so frequently the thing that I hear from them."

"That when they worked with X person or Y organization or in Z environment, they learned what great actually is, and that just permanently changed their sense for what their own standard for their work ought to be."

"Maybe one version of what people in their twenties should do is... figure out, where can you learn the highest standards? Where are the highest standards embodied, and where can you go and experience that firsthand?"

@patrickc with @dwarkesh_sp, 2024

tweets.text:
Is this a bubble? No… not yet.

Since 1981, the MACROSHARK Bubble Index has only reached bubble territory at the 1987, 2000, 2007 and 2021 peaks. We're not there.

But 2026 moved it fast. In May it was higher than about 60% of all months since 1981. Today it's higher than 88%.

Readings this high haven't meant the top is in. They've meant the odds tilt: lower returns over the following 12 months, and bigger drawdowns along the way.

The rubber band is stretched, not snapped.

Finally, Happy Thanksgiving to everyone who celebrates!
